title: Votara: on-chain DAO proposals with one vote per wallet, quorum and an approval threshold
summary: Register as a voter, get voting power, create a proposal, vote once, and after the voting period the DAO authority finalizes it as passed or rejected.
what: Votara is a single on-chain DAO. One `Dao` account and one `Config` account hold the rules: voting period, timelock, quorum, approval threshold and title and description limits. Wallets become voters with a `Voter` PDA that carries their voting power. Any voter can open a proposal. Each voter can vote Yes, No or Abstain **once** per proposal, because the vote itself is a PDA of (proposal, voter) that can only be created once. When the voting period is over, the DAO authority finalizes: too few voters means rejected; otherwise Yes as a percentage of all votes must reach the approval threshold. The lesson is about the governance mechanics. The token side is unfinished in the fork: staking and buying **move no tokens and no SOL** and just add voting power, which the lesson treats as a bug to fix.
app_note: The fork's own React + Vite app with this devnet program ID, hash routing (`#/proposals`, `#/create`, `#/treasury`, `#/profile`) and one fix: a token-balance widget read a React context that is never mounted, which blanked the whole app on the profile page. Script: [tests/devnet/patches/votara.py](https://github.com/Blockchains/sol-college/blob/main/tests/devnet/patches/votara.py). The DAO authority is our test wallet m4Ac…; we set the voting period to 150 s, timelock 0 and quorum 2 voters with `update_config` (defaults: 7 days, 2 days, 10).

try_steps.do: Open [the app](/dapps/votara/) and connect a devnet wallet with a little SOL.
try_steps.see: The Votara dashboard: DAO stats, All Proposals, Create Proposal, Treasury, Voter Profile.
One transaction that creates your governance-token account and calls `stake_tokens(0)`, which creates your `Voter` PDA with 0 voting power.
try_steps.ran_note: Not clicked: our test wallet was already a voter (the app shows no Register button then).

try_steps.do: Open **Treasury**, enter `10`, press **Swap SOL for VTR**.
try_steps.see: A `buy_tokens` transaction. Your voting power goes up by 10, but no SOL leaves your wallet and no token arrives: the transfers are placeholders in the program.
ran: Swap SOL for VTR, 10 more (second run)

try_steps.do: Open **Create Proposal**, enter a title (100 characters at most) and a summary, press **Broadcast Proposal**.
try_steps.see: A `create_proposal` transaction; the proposal appears in All Proposals with a 150-second countdown.
ran: Broadcast Proposal, "UI proposal 06006" (40 s voting period)

try_steps.do: Within those 150 s: **All Proposals**, open it, choose **Yes**, press **Confirm Yes Vote**.
try_steps.see: A `cast_vote` transaction adding your voting power to Yes. Voting again fails, because your vote record already exists. The live counter on the page may stay at 0 until you reload: it listens on a websocket log feed.
ran: Yes, Confirm Yes Vote on "UI proposal 06230" (on chain: yes 20, 1 voter)
try_steps.ran_note: On the 40 s proposal the vote came too late: the wallet simulation returned ProposalClosed (6003) and nothing was sent.

try_steps.do: (DAO authority only.) After the period, press **Finalize & Pick Winner**.
try_steps.see: A `finalize_proposal` transaction: with quorum 2, a proposal with one voter is rejected whatever the votes. Other wallets get `Unauthorized`.
ran: Finalize & Pick Winner on the 40 s proposal: no votes → Rejected
Finalize & Pick Winner on "UI proposal 06230": 1 voter < quorum 2 → Rejected

diagram:
authority ─ initialize_dao() ─▶ Dao PDA ["dao"]  +  Config PDA ["config"]   (one DAO per program)
authority ─ initialize_treasury() ─▶ Treasury PDA ["treasury"], gov mint PDA ["governance_mint"], vault PDA ["vault"]
authority ─ update_config(voting_period?, timelock?, quorum?, threshold?, …)
wallet ──── stake_tokens(n) / buy_tokens(n) ─▶ Voter PDA ["voter", wallet]  voting_power = tokens_staked   (no tokens move)
voter ───── create_proposal(id = dao.total_proposals, title, …) ─▶ Proposal PDA ["proposal", id u64 LE] + Analytics PDA ["analytics", proposal]
voter ───── cast_vote(Yes|No|Abstain) ─▶ VoteRecord PDA ["vote", proposal, voter_pda]  (init → once only)
authority ─ finalize_proposal() after end ─▶ unique_voters ≥ quorum ? (yes×100 / all votes ≥ threshold ? Passed : Rejected) : Rejected
accounts: Authority, counters, gov mint and treasury addresses, pause flag
Voting period, timelock, quorum, approval threshold, limits
Title, description, yes/no/abstain totals, unique voters, status, end time
Which way you voted and with how much power; its existence is the one-vote rule
Counters, the gov token mint and a token vault (no tokens are moved yet)

instructions.name: `initialize_dao` and `update_config`: the rules
steps: Fixed seeds `["dao"]` and `["config"]`: there is exactly one DAO per deployed program.
Defaults: 7-day voting, 2-day timelock, `quorum_percentage = 10`, approval threshold 51, titles up to 100 bytes.
`update_config` takes every field as an `Option` and changes only the ones sent. `constraint = dao.authority == authority.key()` makes it authority-only (`Unauthorized` for anyone else, in Proof).

instructions.name: `stake_tokens` / `buy_tokens`: voting power
steps: Both create your `Voter` PDA on first use (`init_if_needed`) and set `voting_power = tokens_staked` (1 token = 1 vote).

The token transfer is a comment (lines 615–616); `buy_tokens` has no transfer at all (line 670). So power is free: B "staked" 100 while holding 0 gov tokens, and the gov supply was still 0 at the end of our run.
`buy_tokens` only checks and decrements the treasury's `total_tokens` counter, which `stake_tokens` increments.

instructions.name: `create_proposal`
steps: The client picks `proposal_id`; the address is `["proposal", id as 8 little-endian bytes]`. The app uses `dao.total_proposals` as the next id.
Title and description lengths are checked against the config (`TitleTooLong`, in Proof).
`end_time = now + voting_period`; an Analytics PDA is created alongside for live counters.

instructions.name: `cast_vote`: one vote per voter, enforced by an account
steps: Refuses after `end_time` (`ProposalClosed`, in Proof, from the script and from the app).
Adds your current `voting_power` to Yes, No or Abstain and increments `unique_voters`.
`vote_record` is `init` at `["vote", proposal, voter]`; a second vote fails because the account already exists (B's second vote, in Proof). No "has voted" flag is needed.

instructions.name: `finalize_proposal`: quorum, then threshold
steps: Only the DAO authority (`Unauthorized`), only after `end_time` (`VotingPeriodNotEnded`), only while Active.
Quorum: `unique_voters >= quorum_percentage`. Despite its name it is a **count of voters**, not a percentage.

Approval = yes × 100 / (yes + no + abstain), integer division, against the threshold. Script: 100 Yes and 40 No from 2 voters → 71 ≥ 51 → **Passed**. UI: 20 Yes from 1 voter → under quorum 2 → **Rejected**.

innovation.title: the vote is an account: PDAs as a uniqueness constraint
innovation.text: Votara enforces one vote per wallet per proposal without storing a list of voters: the vote record lives at a PDA of (proposal, voter) and is created with `init`, so the runtime itself refuses a second one. The same pattern gives every wallet exactly one voter profile (`["voter", wallet]`) and every proposal a predictable address from its number, so the app can find everything without an index.

refs.note: the same seeds in the app

more: Uniqueness of *wallets* is not uniqueness of *people*, and voting power that costs nothing makes the threshold meaningless. In a real DAO, power must come from tokens actually locked in the vault, and quorum should be measured against total power. Exercises 2–3.

frontend.title: PDAs
steps: Every account is derived in the browser; the proposal id is encoded as 8 little-endian bytes to match `proposal_id.to_le_bytes()`.

frontend.title: Register = create the token account + stake 0
steps: Creates the associated token account for the gov mint if it's missing, then adds `stakeTokens(0)` to the same transaction to create the Voter PDA.

frontend.title: Buy, create, vote, finalize
steps: The next proposal id is `dao.totalProposals`.
Vote passes the vote-record PDA that the program will create; Finalize calls `finalizeProposal`, which only works for the authority.

frontend.title: The live feed
steps: `connection.onLogs` on the program id needs a websocket RPC; on a plain HTTP endpoint the counters stay at 0 until you reload, although the votes are on chain.

exercises.title: Compute both outcomes from Proof
steps: Script proposal: 100 Yes, 40 No, 2 voters. UI proposal: 20 Yes, 1 voter. Quorum 2, threshold 51.
exercises.expect: Script: 100 × 100 / 140 = 71 ≥ 51 and 2 ≥ 2 → Passed (the log says `passed`, `quorumReached: true`). UI: 1 < 2 → Rejected before any percentage is computed.

exercises.title: Make voting power cost something
steps: In `stake_tokens`, add the commented SPL `transfer` CPI from `user_token_account` to `vault` (and constrain `user_token_account` to the gov mint and the signer).
Test: stake 100 with 0 tokens.
exercises.expect: It fails with an insufficient-funds token error instead of giving 100 votes, as it did for B (`3J5VmA5c…`).

exercises.title: A real quorum
steps: Change the quorum check to compare total votes cast with a percentage of the treasury's staked total.
exercises.expect: With 140 staked and quorum 10%, 14 power is needed; the field name now matches what it does.

exercises.title: Block the next proposal id
steps: Read `create_proposal.rs` line 51 and App.tsx line 159.
Locally, with `total_proposals = T`, create a proposal with id `T + 1` from a script, then try to create one through the app.
exercises.expect: The script call raises the counter to T + 1, so the app now tries id T + 1, whose PDA already exists: it fails, and keeps failing, because the counter only grows on success. Nobody can create a proposal from the app any more. Fix: derive the id on chain from `dao.total_proposals` with `seeds = [b"proposal", dao.total_proposals.to_le_bytes()]`.

exercises.title: Why delegation can't succeed
steps: Read `voter/delegate_vote.rs` lines 30–37: the delegate account must sit at `["voter", delegate.key()]`, the key of the account itself.
exercises.expect: No account can be the PDA of its own address, so `delegate_vote` always fails the seeds check. Fix: pass the delegate's wallet as an extra account and use `["voter", delegate_wallet.key()]`.

not_covered: Buy, create, vote and finalize were clicked through in the app; a passing proposal (2 voters) and every rejection case were run by script. Register Voter wasn't clicked (our wallet was already a voter). Not exercised: quadratic voting, retract, delegate (it can't succeed, see Exercise 5), cancel, withdraw and rewards; none of the token or SOL transfers exist in the program. The voting period (150 s), timelock (0) and quorum (2) were set by script; the app has no screen for update_config.
